sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: pgx is the highest-performance PostgreSQL driver for Go, used by Cockroach DB, Supabase, and most performance-critical Go services. Unlike the generic database/sql driver, pgx speaks the PostgreSQL wire protocol natively, exposes type-safe scanning for Postgres-specific types (arrays, JSONB, hstore, uuid), and provides pgxpool for connection management tuned to Postgres semantics. Interviewers at companies running Postgres at scale will probe whether you can configure pool health checks, exploit the COPY protocol for bulk inserts, and instrument LISTEN/NOTIFY for real-time features — all things that database/sql cannot do without the pgx adapter.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body: pgxpool.Pool is the production-grade entry point — it manages a pool of *pgx.Conn connections with background health checks and lazy connection acquisition. Each pgx.Conn speaks the PostgreSQL binary protocol, which means no text marshalling of types like []int or pgtype.JSONB — values are transferred as binary, reducing CPU and bandwidth. pgx.CopyFrom streams rows to Postgres using the COPY protocol, which bypasses per-row INSERT parsing and achieves bulk insert speeds of 100k+ rows/second. pgconn.PgConn.Exec (the low-level layer) and pgxpool.Pool.Exec (the high-level layer) both accept context for cancellation. LISTEN/NOTIFY is a Postgres-native pub/sub mechanism accessed via conn.WaitForNotification, useful for cache invalidation or live queries.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body: 1. pgxpool.New vs pgx.Connect — always use pgxpool in services; pgx.Connect is for one-off scripts or migrations. 2. pgxpool.Config fields — MaxConns, MinConns, HealthCheckPeriod, MaxConnIdleTime, ConnConfig. 3. pgtype registry — pgx v5 uses pgtype.NewMap() to register custom codec; built-in support for uuid, timestamptz, []text, JSONB. 4. pgx.CopyFromRows / pgx.CopyFromSource — stream bulk data into Postgres; far faster than batched INSERTs. 5. LISTEN/NOTIFY — conn.Exec(ctx, "LISTEN channel") then conn.WaitForNotification(ctx); requires a dedicated long-lived connection outside the pool. 6. pgxpool.Pool.AcquireFunc — borrows then returns a connection safely in a closure. 7. EXPLAIN ANALYZE from Go — run as a normal db.QueryRow, parse the returned text or JSON plan. 8. Index strategy — B-tree for equality/range, GIN for JSONB/full-text, BRIN for append-only time-series tables.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body: Q: Why use pgx instead of the standard lib/pq driver? — pgx is actively maintained, supports binary protocol (faster, less CPU), native Postgres types, COPY protocol, and pgxpool. lib/pq is in maintenance mode. Q: How does pgx.CopyFrom compare to batched INSERTs? — CopyFrom uses Postgres COPY protocol, skipping per-row parse/plan/execute cycles; typically 5-10x faster for bulk loads. Q: How would you implement a real-time notification system with Postgres and Go? — LISTEN/NOTIFY: one goroutine holds a dedicated pgx.Conn listening on a channel, forwarding payloads to application subscribers. Q: What pgxpool settings matter most for a high-throughput API? — MaxConns (cap at db server limit divided by replicas), MinConns (warm pool baseline), HealthCheckPeriod (detect stale connections), MaxConnIdleTime. Q: How do you run EXPLAIN ANALYZE from Go? — Execute it as a normal query with db.QueryRow; use the JSON format for programmatic parsing of the plan.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: "For any service talking to Postgres in production I use pgxpool rather than database/sql with the pgx adapter, because pgxpool gives me Postgres-native health checks and binary protocol by default. I configure MinConns to pre-warm a small baseline so the first requests after a deploy don't all race to open connections. For bulk data ingestion — like importing CSV data or syncing from an external API — I always use pgx.CopyFromRows; in benchmarks it's consistently 5-10x faster than batched INSERTs. I use LISTEN/NOTIFY for lightweight cache invalidation between service instances — it avoids polling and the latency is sub-millisecond for local Postgres. When debugging a slow query I run EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, FORMAT JSON) through the same pgxpool and parse the resulting plan in the application so I can log it with the query context."
